children: TOMS Capital Investment Management LP (“TCIM”), which manages funds that together have an investment representing an approximately 4.5% economic interest in Voya Financial, Inc. (

) (“Voya” or the “Company”), today commented on the results of the vote on a non-binding resolution put forward by TCIM, which provided shareholders the opportunity to convey unequivocally that they “no longer continue to have confidence in the Board of Directors (the “Board”) and management of Voya Financial, Inc.” and believe the Company should launch a public strategic alternatives process.
TCIM issued the following statement:

“At the outset of this campaign, we were fully aware that it would be difficult for the major proxy advisory firms and certain institutional investors to support the referendum, given that this was the first time a campaign of this type has ever been run, and given the binary choice – covering confidence in all Voya management and the Board and directly supporting an immediate public strategic alternatives process – required under its terms.
Based on a preliminary analysis performed by our proxy solicitor, our referendum was only supported by a minority of investors.
That said, our aims for this campaign were threefold:
Shine a spotlight on what we view as entrenched behavior from Voya’s Board and management team, which has not been in the best interests of all shareholders;

Provide shareholders with a structured forum, within the defined regulatory framework overseen by the SEC, to engage with us and share their views, as Voya’s lack of a special meeting provision has historically prevented any other such mechanism; and
Identify the issues and arguments that would resonate with fellow investors and proxy advisory firms in advance of the Annual Meeting next spring, at which directors will be elected.

All three of these goals were achieved. We were also highly encouraged by the fact that so many of Voya’s significant investors dedicated time and resources to understanding our concerns and meeting with us, in spite of our concerns that Voya engaged in unlawful solicitation activities (detailed here) by effectively soliciting shareholders outside of SEC rules while publicly saying there is nothing for it to solicit. Many key shareholders agree that to optimize value creation from the franchise, Voya must be willing to engage with interested counterparties, and these shareholders have also lacked confidence that Voya is willing to do so.

In addition, and perhaps even more importantly, we believe that much of the analysis provided by the leading proxy advisory firms has reinforced our views about Voya. For example, Institutional Shareholder Services Inc. (“ISS”) raised concerns about Voya’s response to the campaign, approach to shareholder communication and the fact that our frustrations resonated with other shareholders:
“TCIM also correctly highlights concerns with the company’s response to this campaign.”
“ISS also engaged with the board. However, the board did not have supporting materials, and it was seemingly unprepared to discuss key topics beyond a cursory level.”

“In discussions with ISS, many shareholders expressed frustration with the company’s failure to publicly engage, and many also questioned the company’s receptiveness to M&A. In other words, the company has done itself no favors by eschewing a substantive response, and it would not necessarily be surprising if this campaign advances to a proxy fight.”
Similarly, Glass Lewis noted Voya’s underperformance for shareholders and the potential benefits of exploring strategic alternatives:
“Voya’s historical underperformance and mixed record of strategic execution provide a reasonable basis for TCIM’s criticisms…”

“The Company has generally lagged its peers in TSR, experienced a material deterioration in its relative valuation, and fallen short of certain operating and acquisition-related expectations, particularly with respect to Benefitfocus and medical stop-loss business.”

“Given these considerations, there may be merit to evaluating strategic alternatives, including a potential sale of the Company or certain businesses, to determine whether such opportunities could deliver greater shareholder value than continued standalone execution.”

We would like to thank everyone that took the time to exchange views with us throughout this process. While our preference continues to be constructive engagement with Voya, we are now more confident than ever that the upcoming AGM – the nomination window for which opens on January 21, 2027 – represents a critical opportunity for catalyzing change at Voya and finally unlocking full value for shareholders.”

Participants in the Solicitation

TCIM and the other Participants (as defined below) expect to file a preliminary proxy statement and accompanying universal proxy card with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) to be used to solicit proxies for, among other matters, the election of the Participants’ slate of director nominees at the 2027 annual meeting of stockholders of Voya (the “Proxy Statement”). The participants in the proxy solicitation are currently anticipated to be TCIM, TCIM Master Fund Ltd., TCIM Management GP LLC, Benjamin Pass, and Akash Bagaria (collectively, the “Participants”)

As of November 24, 2026, TCIM Master Fund Ltd. has beneficial ownership of or owns derivative securities with economic exposure to 1,664,160 shares of common stock of Voya, par value $0.01 per share. As of November 24, 2026, TCIM, as investment advisor, may be deemed to beneficially own shares or derivative securities with economic exposure 3,974,807 shares of common stock of Voya, par value $0.01 per share, owned by the persons it advises. As of November 24, 2026, TCIM Management GP LLC, as the general partner of TCIM, may be deemed to beneficially own or have economic exposure to 3,974,807 shares of common stock of Voya, par value $0.01 per share, owned directly or underlying derivative securities owned by the persons TCIM advises.
